rationale: Ground truth has no substantive reviewer concerns, so recall is trivially satisfied by both. X delivers a clean, accurate review with one valid but softly-stated nit (sm_110a exclusion), verified via grep for the rename. Y performs deeper, more grounded verification (traces actual call sites like install_quack_fp8_patch/patch.py, checks for duplicate helpers, confirms test correctness against real entry points) and surfaces an additional genuinely valuable, well-grounded finding X missed entirely: the new doc text implies VLLM_OMNI_USE_QUACK_FP8=1 fixes sm_120, but per the diff's own test-file comments CuteDSL doesn't support sm_120a yet, so the override wouldn't actually help. Y's comments also give more concrete file:line + suggested-edit actionability than X's single hedged optional nit.
